- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., >50% negative values) in recent history, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 3-day avg), model often overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2% below prior peak.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.00 values), model tends to overestimate — apply downward bias of 3–5% to 30d forecast.
- If model forecast is >15% above recent 18-day average, check sentiment: if sentiment is weak or mixed, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of sharp decline after peak), model often fails to adjust — apply lag correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.33/1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before final output.
